title: Demonstrating Bix's Sweet Sue bridge
summary: Hug demonstrates Bix's ninth-chord bridge to show it was worked out at the piano.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, do you want to try a Bix solo? Or would that...
You want to do something? A Bix solo? Yeah. You want to... Could you... Should I have that thing on a sweet suit that I was talking about? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
You want to talk about what you mentioned? Yeah. You talked about it too. Yeah. Especially that part you mentioned. What is he doing in that that you especially want to bring to?

Well, I believe you had asked me, John, if he used the piano, you know, and that's right. He did tell me that he did basically use a lot of piano when he was thinking of these solos. And I can find this evident in the great solo that he took on Sweet Soup, particularly in the bridge. I'll just give you an example of it, and then I'll play most of the solo that I can recall right now. Okay. But the bridge was... Let's see if I can get an R. There. Is that what you... That... He's got... Right there. He goes down from...
There. Right there. Yeah. Is that what you... What's going on right there? He's got... Right there. He goes down from... To an E flat ninth chord, you see?
